response.answer: Effective occupational safety and health interventions benefit from an ecosystem perspective, integrating cross-national strategies and expert insights. Studies emphasize the importance of multi-level collaboration and adaptive policies for optimal outcomes. Research highlights the role of comprehensive, interconnected approaches in enhancing workplace safety globally.

results.title: The Ecosystem Approach to Opioid Policy - RAND
results.content: RAND researchers provide a tool to help federal, state, and local policymakers better understand America's opioid ecosystem.

results.title: The beneficial workplace - Mercer
results.content: Emily Ferreira speaks with Mercer’s Director of Research for Health and Benefits, Beth Umland, about what is contributing to the highest healthcare cost growth in 15 years and how employers are responding. Listen as Emily Ferreira speaks with Chief Health Actuary Sunit Patel on Mercer’s preliminary projection for 2026 health benefit cost growth - and what employers can do about it. In the latest installment of the Beneficial Workplace podcast, host Emily Ferreira sits down with Kate Brown, leader of Mercer’s Center for Health Innovation, to discuss how AI is currently integrated into health benefit programs, the increasing usage of agentic AI in benefits administration and how AI will continue to evolve within the healthcare sphere in the years to come. For the full webinar, [click here](https://www.mercer.com/en-us/insights/events/breakthrough-strategies-to-slow-health-cost-growth/). Host Emily Ferreira speaks with inclusive benefits specialist Lindsay Bower on Mercer survey data in the area of women’s health and how employers are addressing their needs today, where gaps remain and what we see for future offerings.

results.content: Beginner’s Guide – Preparedness for High-Consequence Infectious Diseases***Kelly Yascheshyn, BScN, RN, MICN, CEN, NHDP-BC, Clinical Educator, Disaster, and Danisha Jenkins, Sharpe Healthcare*High Consequence Infectious Diseases (HCID) and Emerging Special Pathogens pose considerable risks to a hospital’s care delivery continuum, to the safety of their staff, and their reputation within the community. Kathy Harris is the Executive Director of the Office of Emergency Management, serving Stanford Health Care and Stanford Medicine Children’s Health in many planned and unplanned incident responses including new hospital activations, pandemic, work stoppage, infrastructure outages, severe weather, wildfire, and supply shortage. In addition to practicing pediatric hospital medicine at Lucile Packard Children’s Hospital, she serves as the Assistant Medical Director for the Office of Emergency Management for both the Stanford Medicine Children’s Health and Stanford Health Care enterprises. He serves as Chair of the Southern California Pediatric Disaster Coalition, Chair of the Health Care Coalition of Orange County’s Hospital Advisory Committee, and co-chair of the Emergency Preparedness Interagency Collaborative’s (EPIC) Hospital Liaison Group.
